claims.text: The identity of X (Al, Si, or Mn) governs whether CrFeCoNiX forms and maintains a stable protective oxide scale above 900 °C.
Al has sufficiently strong oxygen affinity and low volatility to promote formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale on CrFeCoNiAl.
Si has sufficiently strong oxygen affinity and low volatility to promote formation of a continuous, adherent SiO2 scale on CrFeCoNiSi.
Continuous Al2O3 or SiO2 scales act as effective diffusion barriers during high-temperature exposure.
Mn is a major oxide-forming element in CrFeCoNiMn and produces non-protective surface oxides.
Mn oxides formed on CrFeCoNiMn are volatile.
Mn oxide scales are prone to cracking and spallation.
Oxidation of CrFeCoNiMn causes bulk Mn depletion.
A homogeneous single-phase solid solution promotes more uniform oxide growth than a multiphase microstructure.
Elemental partitioning in multiphase CrFeCoNiX disrupts oxide-scale continuity.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will have lower oxidation mass gain than CrFeCoNiMn and the CrFeCoNi baseline.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will form more continuous and adherent scales with fewer cracks and spalls than CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNi.
Mn-containing variants will undergo greater oxidation-induced degradation than Al- or Si-containing variants.
Multiphase variants will exhibit more spallation and degradation than corresponding single-phase variants.
CrFeCoNi without an added X element is the comparison baseline.
The proposed comparison applies to exposure above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Oxidation kinetics, scale continuity, scale thickness, cracking, spallation, phases, and chemistry can be compared using gravimetry, SEM, XRD, TEM, and EDS.
Failure of Al- and Si-containing alloys to improve significantly over both CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNi, or a negligible single-phase versus multiphase difference, would falsify the hypothesis.
